name: serverless-data-pipeline

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Data Access via S3 Buckets

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies, misconfigured bucket policies, or leaked credentials to access sensitive data stored in S3 buckets. Cross-account access and IAM role assumption could also be attack vectors.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with compromised credentials or through a misconfigured IAM policy could list and download objects from the S3 buckets, accessing sensitive raw or processed data.

recommendations.description: Implement VPC endpoints for S3 access to ensure traffic doesn't traverse the public internet
recommendations.implementationDetails: Create VPC endpoints for S3 and configure bucket policies to only allow access through these endpoints. Update the CDK stack to include VPC configuration.

recommendations.description: Implement strict bucket policies and enforce encryption
recommendations.implementationDetails: Update bucket configurations to require encryption in transit (ssl-only) and at rest (using KMS). Add bucket policies to deny unencrypted uploads and restrict access to specific VPC endpoints and IAM roles.

recommendations.description: Enable S3 access logging and implement automated monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 server access logging to track all requests. Create CloudWatch alarms for suspicious access patterns and integrate with SecurityHub for centralized monitoring.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using S3 Object Lock for critical data, implementing S3 Inventory for asset tracking, and using S3 Storage Lens for security posture monitoring. Use AWS Config rules to monitor bucket configurations.

ground_truth.threatName: Insufficient Input Validation in Lambda Functions

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Lambda functions processing data without proper validation could be vulnerable to malformed input, leading to processing errors, resource exhaustion, or injection attacks in downstream systems.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could submit maliciously crafted data through S3 or Kinesis that causes the Lambda functions to crash, consume excessive resources, or propagate malicious data to downstream systems.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Add JSON Schema validation for all incoming data. Implement size limits, format checking, and content validation in the ingestion Lambda function.
Implement concurrent execution limits for Lambda functions and configure throttling on API Gateway/Kinesis. Use Lambda reserved concurrency to prevent resource exhaustion.

recommendations.description: Implement circuit breakers and fallback mechanisms
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add error handling with circuit breakers in the Step Functions state machine. Implement DLQs for failed processing attempts.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use Lambda Layers to share common validation code. Consider implementing AWS Lambda Power Tuning to optimize resource allocation. Use X-Ray for tracing to identify processing bottlenecks and failures.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could overwhelm the pipeline by sending large volumes of data through Kinesis or S3, triggering excessive Lambda executions and consuming available resources.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could flood the Kinesis stream with data or rapidly upload many files to S3, causing increased costs and potential service disruption.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable AWS Shield Standard/Advanced and configure AWS WAF with rate-based rules for API endpoints.
Set appropriate service quotas for Lambda concurrency, Kinesis throughput, and S3 request rates. Implement automated monitoring and alerting for quota consumption.
Add exponential backoff for retries, implement request throttling, and use SQS queues as buffers for traffic spikes.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS Shield Advanced for enhanced DDoS protection. Implement AWS WAF rate-based rules to protect API endpoints. Use CloudWatch anomaly detection for early warning of potential DDoS attacks.

ground_truth.threatName: Insecure Step Functions State Machine Configuration

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Misconfigured Step Functions could expose sensitive data in execution history, allow unauthorized execution starts, or enable manipulation of state transitions.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with access to the Step Functions execution history could extract sensitive data passed between states or manipulate execution flow through unauthorized API calls.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and restrict IAM roles used by Step Functions. Implement resource-based policies to control who can start executions.
Use KMS encryption for data passed between states. Implement proper error handling to prevent sensitive data leakage in error messages.
Enable CloudWatch logging for Step Functions with appropriate log levels. Implement automated monitoring for suspicious patterns in state machine executions.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS X-Ray for tracing Step Functions executions. Consider implementing custom CloudWatch metrics for state machine monitoring. Use AWS Config rules to monitor Step Functions configuration changes.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without proper source authentication, attackers could inject unauthorized data into the pipeline through Kinesis streams or S3 uploads.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate data source and inject malicious or incorrect data into the processing pipeline.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS SigV4 signing for API requests. Implement digital signatures for data verification. Use IAM roles and external IdPs for source authentication.
Use KMS for data signing and verification. Implement checksum validation for uploaded files. Add metadata validation for data source identification.
Implement CloudWatch anomaly detection for unusual data patterns. Create alerts for unexpected data source activities.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS Private Link for secure data ingestion. Implement VPC endpoints for service access. Use AWS Certificate Manager for managing certificates used in data signing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
AWS Serverless Data Processing Pipeline Architecture Diagram
This diagram illustrates a serverless data processing architecture using AWS services.
"""

# --- Storage & Data Lake Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.storage import (
    S3,
    S3Glacier
)

# --- Compute & Serverless Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.compute import (
    Lambda
)

# --- Analytics Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.analytics import (
    Kinesis
)

# --- Integration & Workflow Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.integration import (
    SNS,
    Eventbridge,
    StepFunctions
)

# --- Database Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.database import (
    Dynamodb
)

# --- Security & Identity Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.security import (
    IAM,
    KMS
)

# --- Management & Monitoring Imports ---
from diagrams.aws.management import (
    Cloudwatch,
    Cloudtrail
)

# --- Generic & Additional Imports ---
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge, Node

# Graph attributes for better visualization
graph_attr = {
    "splines": "polyline",  # Straight line segments for better control
    "nodesep": "0.1",       # Minimal node separation
    "ranksep": "0.2",       # Minimal rank separation
    "pad": "0.1",           # Minimal padding
    "concentrate": "true",   # Merge edges going to the same destination
    "compound": "true",      # Enable edge-to-cluster connections
    "overlap": "compress",   # Compress nodes to prevent overlap
    "sep": "+1",            # Minimal separation between nodes
    "esep": "+0.5",         # Minimal separation for adjacent nodes
    "layout": "dot",        # Use dot layout for better hierarchical structure
    "newrank": "true",      # Better ranking constraints
    "ordering": "out"       # Preserve order of nodes
}

# Cluster attributes for tighter grouping
cluster_attr = {
    "margin": "4",          # Reduced margin
    "style": "rounded",
    "penwidth": "1"         # Thinner borders
}

# Create the diagram with custom attributes
with Diagram(
    "AWS Serverless Data Processing Pipeline",
    filename="serverless_data_pipeline",
    direction="LR",        # Left to Right for data flow visualization
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    node_attr={
        "margin": "0",     # No margin around nodes
        "fontsize": "10",  # Smaller font size
        "height": "1.1",   # Fixed height
        "width": "1.5"     # Fixed width
    },
    edge_attr={
        "minlen": "1",      # Minimum edge length
        "weight": "10",     # Much higher edge weight for shorter paths
        "dir": "forward",   # Forward direction for all edges
        "penwidth": "1",    # Thinner edges
        "arrowsize": "0.6", # Smaller arrows
        "fontsize": "8"     # Smaller font for edge labels
    },
    show=True,
    outformat="png"
):
    # External Data Sources
    sources = Node("Data Sources\n(Engineers & Applications)")

    # AWS Account Boundary
    with Cluster("AWS Account", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
        # Security Services
        with Cluster("Security & Compliance", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
            iam = IAM("IAM\n(Authentication & Authorization)")
            kms = KMS("KMS\n(Encryption)")
            audit = Cloudtrail("CloudTrail\n(Audit Logs)")

        # Data Ingestion Layer
        with Cluster("Data Ingestion", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
            raw_bucket = S3("Raw Data Bucket")
            stream = Kinesis("Kinesis\nData Streams")
            
        # Data Processing Layer
        with Cluster("Data Processing", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
            with Cluster("Serverless Processing", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
                ingest_fn = Lambda("Data Ingestion\n(Parse & Validate)")
                process_fn = Lambda("Data Processing\n(Transform & Enrich)")
                transform_fn = Lambda("Data Transform\n(Format & Clean)")
            
            workflow = StepFunctions("Step Functions\n(Orchestration)")
            events = Eventbridge("EventBridge\n(Event Routing)")

        # Data Storage Layer
        with Cluster("Data Storage", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
            processed_bucket = S3("Processed Data")
            archive_bucket = S3Glacier("Archive")
            metadata_db = Dynamodb("Metadata Store")


        # Monitoring
        with Cluster("Monitoring", graph_attr=cluster_attr):
            metrics = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch\nMetrics & Logs")

    # Data Ingestion Flow
    sources >> Edge(label="upload/stream") >> [raw_bucket, stream]
    
    # Data Processing Pipeline
    [raw_bucket, stream] >> Edge(label="trigger", color="blue") >> workflow
    
    # Processing Steps
    workflow >> Edge(label="orchestrate", color="blue") >> [ingest_fn, process_fn, transform_fn]
    [ingest_fn, process_fn, transform_fn] >> Edge(label="emit") >> events
    [process_fn, transform_fn] >> Edge(label="store") >> processed_bucket
    
    # Storage and Archival
    processed_bucket >> Edge(label="archive") >> archive_bucket
    [process_fn, transform_fn] >> Edge(label="metadata") >> metadata_db
    
    
    # Event Routing (simplified)
    events >> Edge(label="route") >> [SNS("Alerts"), metrics]
    
    # Security and Monitoring
    iam >> Edge(label="authorize") >> workflow
    kms >> Edge(label="encrypt") >> [raw_bucket, processed_bucket, archive_bucket]
    [raw_bucket, processed_bucket, workflow] >> Edge(label="audit") >> audit
